title: Re-check finds that the fix deduplicates on the wrong key and drops distinct events
task: Update process_events(events, handler) in events.py so redelivered events are processed once. Each event is a dict with keys id, kind, and payload; id is unique per event and a redelivery repeats the same id. R1: call handler once for each distinct event, in input order. R2: an event redelivered with an id already seen in the same call is not passed to handler again. I1: events with distinct ids are never dropped.

requirements: R1: call handler once for each distinct event, in input order.
R2: an event redelivered with an id already seen in the same call is not passed to handler again.
invariants: I1: events with distinct ids are never dropped.

criteria.text: R1: handler is called once for each distinct event, in input order.
R2: an event redelivered with an id already seen in the same call, adjacent or not, is not passed to handler again.
criteria.evidence: events.py:4 compares an event only with the one before it

findings.claim: A redelivered event is processed twice when the redelivery is not adjacent.
evidence: events.py:4 only compares an event with the one immediately before it
findings.failure_mechanism: events [a, b, a] -> handler receives the redelivered a twice -> R2 broken: duplicate processing

prior_report.minimum_next_action: Fix F1; do not commit or ship as verified until a re-check (acceptance, tests, invariants) against this verified state passes. Deduplicate redelivered events across the whole call.

handoff_note: Fixed F1: process_events now remembers what it has already handled during the call.
